name: Cilantro

schedule.notes: Doesn't transplant well. Sow every 2 to 3 weeks for steady supply.
Fall crop runs longer than spring before bolting.
Cut outer stems at the base. Bolts fast in heat — use it before the flower spike opens.

harvest.cues: Leaves are bright green, dissected, before any flower stalk appears. Once it bolts, let it set seed for coriander.
harvest.storageNotes: Stems in a jar of water in the fridge. Or freeze chopped in ice cubes with oil or water.

varieties.name: Calypso
varieties.notes: Bred for slow bolting — the most reliable for spring.

notes: Bolts almost immediately when soil hits 75 F. Plant in partial shade in late spring, or skip summer entirely and run a fall crop. Let some go to seed — coriander is the dried seed and the flowers feed beneficials.
